title: GPS coordinates enable direct identification of child's location
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted to the backend can be directly linked to a specific individual (the child), enabling precise location tracking and identification without additional identifiers.
assumptions: GPS data is inherently tied to the child's device and identity

title: Unauthorized access to child's location data
description: Live GPS coordinates stored or processed by the backend may be accessed by unauthorized parties, including malicious actors, compromised system administrators, or through data breaches.
assumptions: Backend systems may have vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Excessive location data collection
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted at regular intervals may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles. Continuous tracking of a child's movements may be more intrusive than required.
assumptions: The stated purpose may not justify continuous real-time location tracking

title: Linkability of GPS data to other personal information
description: GPS coordinates can be linked with other data about the child (e.g., school schedules, home addresses, social media activity) to create a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and habits.
assumptions: Other data sources may exist that can be correlated with location data

title: Potential non-compliance with location data regulations
description: Collection and processing of children's location data may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other privacy regulations that impose strict requirements for location data, especially for minors.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for children's location data are stringent and may not be fully met
uncertainty_note: Regulatory landscape varies by jurisdiction; specific compliance status unknown

title: Unnecessary Location Data Storage
description: Backend stores location pings in Location History Store, potentially violating data minimization principle. Location data is highly sensitive personal data that may not be strictly required for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Location data is being collected and stored beyond what is necessary for the app's core functionality.

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Stored location pings can be linked to identify individual users and their movement patterns over time, enabling profiling and tracking.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to identify individuals and their movements.

title: Location Data Identifiability
description: Location history can be used to identify individuals through their unique movement patterns, even without explicit identifiers.
assumptions: Movement patterns are unique enough to identify individuals.

title: Location Data Linking to Individual Identity
description: Location pings forwarded from Mobile App Backend to Geofencing Engine can be linked to specific users, enabling tracking of movement patterns and potentially revealing sensitive personal information about daily routines, locations visited, and associations.
assumptions: Location data is personally identifiable and can be correlated with user identity through device identifiers or account associations.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for linking threats; applied based on context of location data transfer.

title: Unnecessary Location Data Disclosure to Geofencing Engine
description: Location pings are transferred from Mobile App Backend to Geofencing Engine. This represents explicit data disclosure that may violate the minimality principle if the Geofencing Engine receives more location data than strictly required for zone entry/exit detection.
assumptions: The Geofencing Engine may have access to location data beyond what is needed for its specific function, or the data may be retained longer than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for data disclosure; applied based on the Process→Process data transfer described in the flow.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance in Location Data Processing
description: The transfer of location pings between processes may violate GDPR or other privacy regulations regarding sensitive personal data, particularly if proper consent, data minimization, or purpose limitation controls are not implemented.
assumptions: Location data is considered sensitive personal data under applicable privacy regulations; the system may not have adequate legal basis or safeguards for this data transfer.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a standard LINDDUN Pro node for non-compliance; applied based on the sensitive nature of location data and regulatory requirements.

title: Linkability of Geofencing Notifications
description: The Geofencing Engine could emit multiple arrival/departure notifications that an external entity could link together to reconstruct the child's movement patterns and location history, potentially revealing sensitive behavioral information.
assumptions: External entity has access to multiple notification instances and can correlate them by time/location
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Location Notifications
description: The geofencing notifications containing arrival/departure information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission to the external entity, potentially exposing the child's location data to unintended recipients.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully secured or access controls are insufficient
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows

title: Identification of Child's Location Patterns
description: The notifications could be used to identify the child's routine movement patterns, zone preferences, and behavioral habits, potentially enabling profiling or stalking.
assumptions: External entity can analyze notification patterns over time to identify behavioral patterns
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable node for identification threats in Process->ExternalEntity flows

title: Parent Identity Linked to Child Profile Data
description: The parent's identity can be linked to the child's personal information (name, DOB, school) and geofence zones through the registration process, potentially enabling tracking of the child's location and activities via the parent's account.
assumptions: The system stores parent-child relationship data that can be used to link profiles

title: Child Personal Information Disclosure
description: Child's sensitive personal data (name, DOB, school) and geofence zones could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through the registration flow, potentially exposing the child's identity and location patterns.
assumptions: Data transmitted from EE1 to P1 may be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized entities

title: Parent Identity Usurpation
description: An unauthorized actor could usurp the parent's identity to create false child profiles or manipulate geofence zones, potentially leading to false location tracking or privacy violations.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be insufficient to verify parent identity

title: Data Disclosure During Processing
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) could disclose child profile data and geofence zones to unauthorized third parties during processing or storage, violating privacy expectations.
assumptions: P1 may share data with external services or have inadequate access controls

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Child Data
description: The system may fail to comply with child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding collection, storage, and processing of children's personal information and location data.
assumptions: System may not implement required consent mechanisms or data minimization practices

title: Excessive Personal Data Storage in Backend
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) stores comprehensive family account, child profile, and geofence zone data. This may violate the minimality principle if the stored data exceeds what is strictly necessary for the intended functionality, creating avoidable explicit disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: The backend stores more data than minimally required for account management and geofence functionality.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on context [3] about data disclosure and minimality principle; tree_node selection is based on standard LINDDUN Pro structure.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Family Data
description: The backend (P1) stores sensitive family account and child profile data. Without proper access controls, authentication, and authorization mechanisms, unauthorized actors could access or manipulate this personal data.
assumptions: The backend lacks adequate security controls for data access.
uncertainty_note: Tree_node U.1.1 is standard LINDDUN Pro structure for usurpation threats; specific node may vary by implementation.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Stored Profiles
description: The backend (P1) stores child profile and geofence zone data. Without proper integrity controls, this data could be tampered with, leading to incorrect account information or compromised geofence functionality.
assumptions: The backend lacks adequate data integrity mechanisms.
uncertainty_note: Tree_node D.1.1 is standard LINDDUN Pro structure for data integrity threats.

title: Linkability of child's location data to parent
description: Parent (EE1) can link the child's location data to specific individuals through the map view, potentially revealing patterns of movement and associations.
assumptions: Parent has access to the map interface and can correlate location data with known individuals

title: Identifiability of child through location history
description: Location history data can identify the child's routine, habits, and potentially sensitive locations (school, home, medical facilities) even when not explicitly named.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to infer personal information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location to third parties
description: Mobile App Backend (P1) may disclose child's location data to unauthorized third parties, including advertisers, analytics services, or other external entities.
assumptions: P1 has data sharing capabilities and may transmit location data beyond the parent's view

title: Non-compliance with location data privacy regulations
description: Processing of child's location data may violate GDPR, COPPA, or other privacy regulations regarding minors' location tracking and parental consent requirements.
assumptions: Applicable privacy laws require specific consent and data minimization for location data of minors

title: Location History Identifiability
description: Stored location history data can be directly linked to specific individuals, revealing their movement patterns and potentially exposing sensitive personal information about their habits, routines, and whereabouts.
assumptions: Location data is inherently personally identifiable and can be correlated with other data sources

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Location history data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during retrieval by the backend process, potentially exposing sensitive movement patterns to third parties or malicious actors.
assumptions: Access controls may not be properly enforced during data retrieval

title: Location Data Usurpation
description: Location history data could be used to impersonate or track an individual's movements, potentially enabling stalking, surveillance, or unauthorized tracking of the data subject.
assumptions: Location data can be used to reconstruct movement patterns and potentially track individuals

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Location Data
description: Processing of location history data may violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA, etc.) regarding sensitive personal data, particularly concerning consent, data minimization, and purpose limitation requirements.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable privacy regulations

title: Location Data Linkability
description: Location history data retrieved by the backend can be linked with other data sources (e.g., device IDs, timestamps, user profiles) to create comprehensive profiles of individuals' movements and behaviors.
assumptions: Backend may have access to or can correlate with other data sources

title: Parent identity linked with child location data
description: When the parent invites a secondary guardian, the system may link the parent's identity with the child's location data, creating a privacy risk where the parent's association with the child's location is exposed.
assumptions: The system tracks which parent initiated the guardian invitation and associates this with the location data being shared.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 based on general linkability methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Parent identified as location data sharer
description: The parent's identity may be revealed through the invitation mechanism, identifying them as the party sharing the child's location with a secondary guardian.
assumptions: The invitation process requires parent authentication and identity confirmation.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 based on general identification methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Child location disclosed to unauthorized guardian
description: The mobile app backend may disclose the child's location to a secondary guardian without proper authorization or consent verification, potentially exposing sensitive location data to unintended parties.
assumptions: The system may not adequately verify the guardian's authorization or the parent's explicit consent before sharing location data.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 based on general disclosure methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Excessive location data retained for guardian access
description: The mobile app backend may retain more location data than necessary for the secondary guardian's access, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The system may store historical location data beyond what is needed for the guardian to view the child's current or recent location.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.1.1 based on general data minimization methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Guardian account compromised enabling location access
description: If the secondary guardian's account is compromised, the mobile app backend may allow unauthorized access to the child's location data through that guardian's credentials.
assumptions: The system relies on guardian account credentials without additional authentication or monitoring for suspicious access patterns.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 based on general usurpation methodology; exact node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The backend shares the child's live location with the secondary guardian, creating a risk that this sensitive data could be further disclosed to unauthorized third parties if the guardian mishandles or leaks the information.
assumptions: The guardian may not have proper safeguards in place to protect the location data from further unauthorized sharing.

title: Location data linked with other personal information
description: The secondary guardian could potentially link the child's live location data with other information they possess, creating a more detailed profile of the child's movements and habits.
assumptions: The guardian may have access to other data sources that could be correlated with the location information.

title: Child's whereabouts identified through location data
description: Live location data can directly identify the child's current whereabouts, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily routine, school, or home location.
assumptions: Location data inherently contains identifying information about the child's physical presence.

title: Unauthorized access to location data by impostor guardian
description: An unauthorized person could potentially impersonate the secondary guardian and gain access to the child's live location data, compromising the child's safety and privacy.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may not be robust enough to prevent impersonation attacks.

title: Potential violation of privacy regulations
description: Sharing a child's live location with an external entity may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) that require explicit consent and appropriate safeguards for children's personal data.
assumptions: The data sharing arrangement may not have proper legal basis or consent mechanisms in place.

title: Analytics data disclosure to unauthorized third parties
description: Advertising/analytics partner may share or sell the aggregated usage and engagement data to additional third parties beyond the intended scope, potentially exposing user behavior patterns to entities without proper consent or legal basis.
assumptions: Partner has business incentives to monetize data beyond the agreed scope; data may be re-identifiable when combined with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is a general disclosure node; specific partner contract terms would determine exact risk level.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in data sharing
description: Sharing aggregated analytics with external advertising partner may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations if data is not properly anonymized, if consent was not obtained, or if data minimization principles are not followed.
assumptions: User consent for analytics sharing may not cover third-party advertising partners; aggregated data may still contain quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on user location and data characteristics; tree node Nc.1.1 is a general non-compliance node.

title: Linkability of aggregated analytics across datasets
description: Even aggregated usage and engagement data may be linkable when combined with other datasets held by the advertising partner or other entities, potentially enabling re-identification of individual users through correlation attacks.
assumptions: Advertising partners typically have access to multiple data sources; aggregation may not be sufficient to prevent linkage when combined with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Risk depends on aggregation granularity and partner's data ecosystem; tree node L.1.1 is a general linkability node.

title: Location data enables child identification
description: The child's current location data in the check-in/SOS message can be used to identify the child's physical whereabouts and potentially link to their identity.
assumptions: Location data is precise enough to identify the child's location

title: Location data disclosed to unauthorized parties
description: The child's location data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through the mobile app backend or during transmission.
assumptions: The system may not have proper access controls

title: Excessive location data collection
description: The check-in/SOS message may collect more precise location data than necessary for the intended purpose of parent notification.
assumptions: The system collects GPS coordinates rather than approximate location

title: Child identity usurpation in SOS message
description: An unauthorized person could potentially send a check-in/SOS message on behalf of the child, impersonating them.
assumptions: The system lacks proper authentication for SOS messages
